svg.title: Souls and Simulacra build-system design pass over the SS2-derived skeleton
svg.desc: A systems diagram for the Souls and Simulacra design pass, guided by the standing Achintya Bheda Abheda ideal that meaningful continuity and real mechanically legible distinction coexist at the same operative relationship rather than being distributed tokenly across separate entries. It shows Bound Soul as a materially required qualitative Relic-grammar lens but not a qualifying weave source, sixteen Rule-Capacity item hosts, Team Tactic, and a late-game Soul Relic weave that requires a bearer source, may include allies, supports all six history/state/cross-form by action/build recipe cells, contains both definition-stable and within-cell instance-variable Relics, and requires every functional input-Charm definition to participate materially in at least one of those cells while remaining stable between comparable same-definition instances inside a fixed cell. Every materially operative Relic instance-state realization must retain a Bound-Soul resonance witness, player-semantic result identity aligns exactly with pre-payoff consumer identity, and some but not all positive contexts have reachable co-result states with a global maximum of two simultaneous receipts. Every supported Bound Soul paired with every materially operative Relic realization has access to a dual weave with an empty input-Charm lane and at least one singleton-grounded foothold. All six cells occur globally, every cell has a singleton exemplar for some exact pair, every exact pair supports at least two native-dual cells, at least one pair supports exactly two, at least one pair/cell edge is absent, and at least one pair/cell edge remains coupled-only. Some but not all exact pairs have a second singleton-backed cell; every fixed exact Relic realization keeps one total cell palette, one one-anchor or multi-anchor class, and one singleton-backed cell count across supported Souls. Every multi-anchor exact realization has some equal-count singleton-label rotation, while every one-anchor realization keeps its sole label stable. Some but not all multi-anchor exact keys distinguish every supported-Soul pair, preserving both pair-complete Soul-identity prisms and affinity-bearing Relics. Every actual unequal-set Soul-pair rotation retains at least one singleton anchor and tightens the supported-Soul ceiling to fifteen. Some but not all multi-anchor keys retain an all-Soul singleton core. C3c.66-A selects exactly two diagonal combinations of pair-completeness and common-core status. C3c.67-A orients them as coreless pair-complete prisms and core-bearing affinities. C3c.68-A gives every affinity exact key exactly one all-Soul core anchor. C3c.69-A makes every multi-support Relic definition prism-pure or affinity-pure. C3c.70-A makes every definition one-/multi-anchor-class-pure. C3c.71-A gives every named Relic one total native-dual cell palette across its exact operative realizations. C3c.72-A gives every named multi-anchor Relic one singleton-anchor count across its exact simulacra. C3c.73-A gives every affinity definition one singleton-map Soul-group count. C3c.74-A gives every affinity definition one unlabeled Soul-group-size profile. C3c.75-A makes every affinity profile fully peer-covered. C3c.76-B makes equal-size and mixed-size affinity names coexist while each name keeps its stable profile. C3c.77-B makes size-role-stable and size-role-variable mixed affinity names coexist. C3c.78-A makes stable mixed names use each group size once, so they are fixed covenants. C3c.79-C makes every equal-size affinity name realize partner-fluid exact Soul partitions, completing a three-dialect vocabulary beside fixed covenants and morphic mixed affinities. C3c.80-A gives every affinity definition one sole all-Soul core cell label across its exact simulacra. C3c.81-A makes every morphic profile use each represented group size once, preserving visible size-role recasting as its distinct dialect. C3c.82-B makes support-positive and forced-breadth affinity definitions coexist. C3c.83-C makes every support-positive affinity realize unequal noncore breadth while forced-breadth names remain stable. C3c.84-B makes some but not all forced-breadth affinities support fixed-breadth exact-union rotation. C3c.85-B makes exactly one of the breathing and fixed-width-capable classes actually realize that rotation. C3c.86-A selects fixed-width-capable-only participation. C3c.87-A makes actually rotating fixed-width names a nonempty proper subset of the capable class. C3c.88-A makes every actual fixed-width union rotation retain at least one noncore motif. C3c.89-B gives exactly one forced-breadth class fixed-union map-family support beyond the breathing class's derived support. C3c.90-B identifies that class as union-locked. C3c.91-B makes locked-class support universal. C3c.92-B makes exactly one eligible class realize actual fixed-union family variation. C3c.93-B identifies that sole actual class as union-locked. C3c.94-B makes actual fixed-union family variation universal within that class. C3c.95-C makes every locked definition all-pairs family-distinguishing. C3c.96-A makes every supported Soul vary somewhere inside every locked definition. C3c.97-C gives every locked definition one common all-Soul-changing exact-key pair. C3c.98-C gives every locked exact key at least one common all-Soul-changing partner. C3c.99-C gives every locked definition structural support for a common pair that preserves and reassigns an exact family member. C3c.100-C makes every locked definition actually author such a pair. C3c.101-C gives every locked exact key an overlap-bearing common partner. C3c.102-C makes every locked definition support two member-disjoint complete noncore map families. C3c.103-C makes every locked definition actually author a member-disjoint common edge. C3c.104-C gives every completed locked exact key structural support for a member-disjoint partner without requiring that partner to be authored. C3c.105-C gives every completed locked exact key both an authored member-disjoint common partner and C3c.101-C's distinct overlap-bearing common partner. C3c.106-C gives every locked definition at least one persistent instance ID across family-different completed snapshots. C3c.107-C gives every completed locked exact key a family-different same-instance partner. C3c.108-C gives every locked definition at least one same-instance one-coordinate comparison. C3c.109-C gives every represented persistent instance ID such a comparison. C3c.110-C gives every locked definition at least one key-complete represented instance. C3c.111-C makes every represented persistent instance-ID fiber key-complete, equivalently giving every completed locked exact key a family-distinct same-ID one-coordinate partner. C3c.112-C keeps both state-only and boundary-only comparison types in the completed locked catalog. C3c.113-A separates those types by definition, so every locked name is state-supporting only or boundary-supporting only and both classes exist. C3c.114-C gives every locked definition at least one represented same-ID fiber containing an all-Soul-changing common edge. C3c.115-C extends that incidence to every represented persistent-instance fiber. C3c.116-C gives every locked definition at least one represented instance fiber whose every completed key has an internal all-Soul-changing partner. C3c.117-C extends that coverage to every represented instance fiber and therefore every completed key. C3c.118-C gives every locked definition at least one exact edge that is both its sole one-coordinate comparison type and an all-Soul-changing common relation. C3c.119-C extends exact alignment to every represented persistent-instance fiber. C3c.120-C gives every locked name at least one represented artifact whose every completed form participates in an aligned edge. C3c.121-C extends aligned-edge participation to every represented artifact and completed form. C3c.122-C keeps both overlap-bearing and member-disjoint identities among actual aligned edges. C3c.123-C fills all four comparison-type by aligned-family cells. C3c.124-A keeps every locked definition aligned-family-pure and forces nonempty S-O, S-R, B-O, and B-R name classes. C3c.125-C gives every locked name at least one same-owner, same-persistent-artifact lived aligned foil. C3c.126-C extends that lived-edge incidence to every represented persistent instance. C3c.127-C gives every locked name at least one represented artifact whose complete key set is covered by lived aligned edges. C3c.128-C extends that coverage to every represented artifact and completed locked form. C3c.129-C gives every locked name at least one represented artifact whose complete form set materially occurs within one qualifying history. C3c.130-C extends that one-history completeness to every represented artifact. C3c.131-A makes every input-affecting Relic-owned state lineage-carried across ordinary encounter cuts. C3c.132-A carries that remembered state across clean Circuit cuts absent a separate state operation. C3c.133-A gives successful results no post-completion participant response window. C3c.134-A seals every provisionally complete aligned receipt candidate against automatic semantic revocation before commitment. C3c.135-A requires relationship insufficiency before a same-tag receipt can rearm. C3c.136-A gives every tag some same-encounter break-renew-recommit path. C3c.137-A forbids every decision-unexposed blink rearm. C3c.138-A requires a material live-context/false opportunity on every recommit path. C3c.139-A requires every path to expose predicate or recurrence leverage while that context stays operative in both isolated alternatives. C3c.140-A requires an alternative actually selected on every path to participate in that leverage. C3c.141-A requires every path to isolate at least one chosen-arm decisive input to predicate facts or recurrence control. C3c.142-C requires global independent support for both predicate and recurrence forms. C3c.143-C makes dual-form and specialist fixed context/receipt tags coexist. C3c.144-A gives every dual tag at least one actual recommit history exercising both independent forms. C3c.145-A makes every legal path of every dual tag both-form. C3c.146-C requires both predicate-only and recurrence-only specialist classes beside the dual class. C3c.147-A gives every candidate tag at least one continuous-context recommit history. C3c.148-A makes every legal recommit history continuous in the post-c1 through pre-q2 slice. C3c.149-A gives every dual tag at least one same-opportunity independent-form history. C3c.150-A puts a joint opportunity on every legal dual-tag history. C3c.151-A gives every dual tag at least one same-decisive-cut convergence history. C3c.152-A puts a same-cut joint opportunity on every legal dual-tag history. C3c.153-A gives every joint opportunity a common predicate/recurrence decisive cut. C3c.154-A makes complete predicate and recurrence cut sets equal at every joint opportunity. C3c.155-A makes every such common set a singleton. C3c.156-A gives both independent forms catalog-level authorized pre-choice support. C3c.157-A gives every mechanically dual tag at least one authorized pre-choice form account. C3c.158-A gives every mechanically dual tag both authorized pre-choice form accounts, possibly on different histories. C3c.159-A gives every mechanically dual tag a same-history two-form disclosure witness. C3c.160-A gives every exact legal history of every mechanically dual tag at least one authorized pre-choice form account. C3c.161-A gives every such history both authorized form accounts, possibly at different opportunities. C3c.162-A gives every dual tag at least one same-opportunity co-legible choice. C3c.163-A gives every exact legal history of every dual tag at least one such choice. C3c.164-A gives every mechanically joint opportunity at least one qualifying pre-choice form. C3c.165-A makes both distinct forms co-legible at every mechanically joint opportunity. C3c.166-A gives every dual tag at least one integrated semantic account relating both forms. C3c.167-A gives every exact legal history an integrated opportunity. C3c.168-A gives every mechanically joint opportunity an integrated account. C3c.169-A gives every dual tag at least one same-history pair of distinct joint opportunities. C3c.170-A gives every dual tag at least one such pair that reuses one canonical integrated-account identity. C3c.171 is active and paused for a macro-index review; it asks whether every multi-opportunity history contains some reuse edge, every dual tag mixes reuse-positive and reuse-negative multi-opportunity histories, or saturated and history-mixed tag classes coexist.
svg.text: Souls and Simulacra — build-system design pass
Standing ideal: continuity + real distinction together • amber = pending • blue = recommendation
Grammar lens; never a weave source
Not assumed to be a Relic source
Nothing here silently supplies a source
Legendary behaviors—and any Forms, Signatures, or Keystones—live inside these items.
Relics and Charms consume neither these hosts nor Rule Capacity; their fixed lanes are complete accounting.
LATE-GAME RELIC WEAVE — PERSONAL, DISCRETE ITEMS
1 RELIC • 2 OPTIONAL CHARMS • NO EXTRA BUDGET
COMPLEMENTARY PAIR • FIXED LANES • BOTH OPTIONAL
both modify the sole active root
Every operative Relic realization has a material Bound-Soul resonance witness
never a configuration gate, scalar bonus, or qualifying weave source
Relic evaluates the authored relationship across qualifying source records
C170-A: one account returns somewhere • C171 PAUSED: every multi-history?
One focal Relic; up to two dependent Charm customizers.
Strongest visual hierarchy and clearest build identity.
B — UP TO TWO ROOTS • NOT SELECTED
ILLUSTRATIVE VISUAL GROUP • NOT A HOST DECISION
Can look like one system, but mechanically creates two
weave graphs and two Bound-Soul resonance pairs.
Presentation can contain complexity; it cannot erase it.
C — NO RELIC-FAMILY CAP • NOT SELECTED
Three-root builds must be real; another later rule must
still prove a finite active state.
PRESENTATION PRINCIPLE • NOT A SELECTED HOST
Keep Relic controls visually grouped and subordinate to equipment.
Exact screen, control placement, and saved configuration remain later.
